lesson.title: Case: reject an unsupported compliance claim
lesson.summary: Find the gaps in a fictional supplier pitch.

prerequisites.reason: The case must specify evidence for the identified gap.
The common-specification claim requires a reasoned equivalence check.
The case includes a cybersecurity certificate with limited coverage.

blocks: **Case pitch:** Northbridge's vendor says, 'Our ISO certificate, a cited logging standard and a cybersecurity certificate make your whole recruitment product compliant.' The exercise stipulates that the logging citation is genuine and the cybersecurity scheme qualifies, but both cover limited requirements.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 40–42; Annex IV(7)

blocks: Separate the claims. The ISO certificate concerns its stated organisational scope. Logging evidence concerns its stated covered requirement. The cybersecurity evidence concerns only the specified cybersecurity coverage. None automatically settles Northbridge's data, oversight or complete procedure.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 40–42; Annex IV(7)

blocks: Request a coverage matrix and implementation evidence. For uncovered requirements obtain detailed compliance solutions and results. If an applicable common specification is not followed, add the duly justified equivalent-level comparison. Do not treat a supplier's commercial warranty as the missing technical evidence.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 40–42; Annex IV(7)

blocks: Case conclusion: **not ready on the evidence presented**. Record the gaps and follow-up owner. This conclusion concerns the incomplete pitch; it does not establish that the underlying product could never satisfy the law.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 40–42; Annex IV(7)
